items.title: The observer split of a symmetric two-tensor: energy density, energy-momentum current, flux and stress
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
subset carrying the restricted smooth structure of
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]],
let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), and let $n$ be a smooth observer
congruence on $U$ ([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]), so that
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $n_p$ is future-directed at every $p\in U$.

**(a) Spatial projection field.** Let

$$h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$$

on $U$, the component expression of the field of $g$-orthogonal projections
onto the rest spaces $n_p^{\perp}$ of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]
([[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]); at every $p$ one has
$h^a{}_bn^b=0$, $n_a h^a{}_b=0$, $h^a{}_bh^b{}_c=h^a{}_c$ and
$h^a{}_a=3$. The field is smooth because $n$, $g$ and the identity are smooth
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]).

**(b) Measured energy density.** The **measured energy density** of $T$ for the
congruence $n$ is the smooth function

$$\mu:=T_{ab}n^an^b:U\to\mathbb R .$$

**(c) Energy-momentum current.** The **energy-momentum current** of $T$ for the
congruence $n$ is the smooth vector field on $U$ obtained by raising one index
of $T$ with the inverse metric and contracting with $n$,

$$J^a:=-T^{ab}n_b,$$

with $T^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}T_{cd}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]); the minus sign is the convention that
fixes the energy-component sign convention. A positive $\mu$
alone does not imply that $J$ is causal: $J$ may have an arbitrarily large
spatial part. No future-causal property of $J$ is imposed by this definition.

**(d) Energy flux.** The **energy flux** of $T$ for the congruence $n$ is the
smooth vector field

$$\Phi^a:=h^a{}_bJ^b=J^a-\mu n^a,$$

the spatial projection of $J$; it satisfies $n_a\Phi^a=0$ and
$\Phi^a=-h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$.

**(e) Spatial stress.** The **spatial stress** of $T$ for the congruence $n$ is
the smooth field obtained by projecting both tensor slots,

$$S^{ab}:=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd},$$

which is symmetric in $a,b$ and satisfies $S^{ab}n_b=0$.

The identities $\mu=-J^an_a$, $J=\mu n+\Phi$, $S^{ab}n_b=0$ and the orthogonal
decomposition

$$T^{ab}=\mu n^an^b+n^a\Phi^b+n^b\Phi^a+S^{ab},$$

together with the uniqueness of that decomposition and the component formulas
in a $g$-orthonormal frame, are proved in
[[lem-gr-observer-energy-momentum-decomposition]]; this definition asserts
none of them. The physical reading and the units of $\mu$, $\Phi$ and $S$ are
fixed by the framework's reading on this page and are not asserted here.

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), section 4.1.2 '3+1 decomposition of the stress-energy tensor': the energy density E = T(n,n), the momentum density p = -T(n,gamma(.)) and the stress S = gamma*T as measured by the Eulerian observer, printed p. 52 (PDF p. 52)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.3: T_{mu nu}u^mu u^nu = rho as the energy density measured by an observer comoving with the fluid, printed p. 186 (PDF p. 193)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 (1.107)-(1.110): the energy density and pressure reading of the components of the stress-energy tensor, printed pp. 29-30 (PDF pp. 36-37)

items.title: The orthogonal observer decomposition of a symmetric two-tensor and its uniqueness
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset, let $T$ be a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$ and let $n$ be a smooth observer congruence on
$U$, and let $\mu$, $J$, $\Phi$, $S$ and $h$ be as in
[[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]]. Then:

**(a) Smoothness and elementary properties.** $\mu$ is a smooth function, $J$
and $\Phi$ are smooth vector fields and $S$ is a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor
field on $U$; moreover

$$n_a\Phi^a=0,\qquad S^{ab}n_b=0,\qquad \mu=-J^an_a .$$

**(b) Orthogonal decomposition.** The identity of smooth tensor fields

$$T^{ab}=\mu\,n^an^b+n^a\Phi^b+n^b\Phi^a+S^{ab}$$

holds on $U$, together with the contraction identity
$T^{ab}n_a=-\mu n^b-\Phi^b$.

**(c) Uniqueness.** If $\mu'$ is a smooth function, $\Psi$ a smooth vector
field with $\Psi^an_a=0$ and $S'$ a smooth symmetric tensor field with
$S'^{ab}n_b=0$ on $U$, and if

$$T^{ab}=\mu'\,n^an^b+n^a\Psi^b+n^b\Psi^a+S'^{ab},$$

then $\mu'=\mu$, $\Psi=\Phi$ and $S'=S$.

**(d) Values on the rest space and frame components.** For every $p\in U$ and
every $v\in n_p^{\perp}$,

$$T_p(n_p,n_p)=\mu(p),\qquad T_p(n_p,v)=-g_p(\Phi_p,v),$$

so the restriction of $T_p$ to $n_p^{\perp}\times n_p^{\perp}$ agrees with
$S_p$. In every ordered $g_p$-orthonormal basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $T_pM$
with $e_0=n_p$,

$$\mu(p)=T_{00}(p),\qquad \Phi^i(p)=T^{0i}(p)=-T_{0i}(p)\quad(i=1,2,3),$$

and $S^{ij}(p)=T^{ij}(p)$ for $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$ while $S^{0a}(p)=0$. Finally
$g_{ab}S^{ab}=g_{ab}T^{ab}+\mu$.

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), section 4.1.2: the 3+1 decomposition E = T(n,n), p = -T(n,gamma(.)) and S = gamma*T of the stress-energy tensor, printed p. 52 (PDF p. 52), and section 5.2.3, whose remark identifies p with the energy flux, printed p. 74 (PDF p. 74)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 (1.107)-(1.110): the component reading of the stress-energy tensor in a rest frame, printed pp. 29-30 (PDF pp. 36-37)

items.title: Physical reading of the observer split: measured energy density, energy flux and momentum density, and measured stress
items.statement:
Adopt the framework's unit and reading conventions
([[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]) and the stress-energy slot
([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented
smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset,
let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$ and let $n$ be
a smooth observer congruence on $U$
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]). Let $\mu$, $J$, $\Phi$
and $S$ be the fields of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]].

**(a) Measured energy density and its unit.** The smooth function
$\mu=T_{ab}n^an^b$ is read as the **energy density measured by the observers of
the congruence $n$**, with numerical values in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ when
$T$ is read in the orthonormal-frame convention of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]] clauses (a) and (d). The same item fixes
the energy-density reading of $\rho_n=T(n,n)$ for a future unit timelike
$n$.

**(b) Energy flux and momentum density.** The smooth spatial vector field
$\Phi=h(J)$ of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]] is the tensor's
spatial current in the normalized observer convention. Its components have
energy-density units, $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. Define the **SI measured
energy-flux vector** $q:=c\Phi$ and **SI measured momentum-density covector**
$p:=\Phi^{\flat}/c$, where $\Phi^{\flat}(a)=g(\Phi,a)$ and $c$ is the
conversion constant of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]].
In every ordered orthonormal basis with future $e_0=n_p$,

$$\Phi^i=T^{0i}=-T(e_0,e_i),\qquad q^i=c\Phi^i,\qquad p_i=\Phi^i/c,\qquad i=1,2,3,$$

by [[lem-gr-observer-energy-momentum-decomposition]] (d). Hence $q^i$ has
units $\mathrm W\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $p_i$ has units
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; equivalently $q^{\flat}=c^2p$.
When the algebraic balance formulas call $\Phi$ an energy flux they use this
normalized tensor current, whose SI energy flux is $c\Phi$. The analogous
natural-unit momentum notation suppresses the factor $1/c$; it never assigns
SI momentum units directly to $\Phi^{\flat}$. Symmetry of $T$ gives the two
aspects of the same mixed component, with these distinct SI conversions.

**(c) Measured stress.** The smooth symmetric field $S=h^*h^*T$ of
[[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]] clause (e) is read as the **stress
measured by the observers** of the congruence: for unit spatial vectors
$e,e'$ in the rest space of $n_p$, $S_p(e,e')$ is read as the force per unit
area in the direction $e$ across a surface whose normal is $e'$, with
components in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ by the conventions.

**(d) Current and charge reading.** For this clause choose an orientation on
$U$ and the volume form of its restricted metric; this choice is independent
of the time orientation. The smooth vector field $J$ of
[[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]] clause (c) is read as the
**energy-momentum current density measured by the congruence**, and for a
finite smooth singular $3$-chain $\Sigma$ of $U$ the flux $\Phi_J(\Sigma)$ of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) is read as the
energy-momentum assigned to $\Sigma$ by the congruence, in the sense of the
charge reading of that item. For a $3$-chain carried by a spacelike slice
whose normal is (up to sign) $n$, the index-lowered component $-J_an^a=\mu$ is
the density integrated in that reading.

**(e) Scope.** The reading is interpretive and applies to every prescribed
smooth symmetric $T$ and every observer congruence. No positivity of $\mu$, no
conservation of $J$, no dynamics, no existence of a matter model realizing $T$
and no measurement is asserted; the definition is confined to the smooth
branch of the framework, and $T$ need not satisfy any field equation.

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), section 4.1.2: E = T(n,n) is the matter energy density and p = -T(n,gamma(.)) the momentum density measured by the Eulerian observer, with S = gamma*T the measured stress, printed p. 52 (PDF p. 52); section 5.2.3: the remark that p plays the role of an energy flux and that both aspects are equivalent, printed p. 74 (PDF p. 74)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.3: T_{mu nu}u^mu u^nu = rho is the energy density measured by an observer comoving with the fluid, printed p. 186 (PDF p. 193); section 4.5.5: the conserved charge of the current -K^mu T_{mu nu} and its energy interpretation for a timelike Killing vector, printed pp. 188-189 (PDF pp. 195-196)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 4: the energy-momentum tensor as the source of the field equation and the reading of its components, printed pp. 116-118 (PDF pp. 123-125)

items.physical_scope: The physical reading of the algebraic observer split of a smooth symmetric two-tensor on the smooth classical branch of the framework: the measured energy density, energy-flux and momentum-density readings and the measured stress of a prescribed tensor for a prescribed observer congruence, with the framework's unit conventions. The item fixes names, component formulas and units only; it asserts no positivity, no conservation, no dynamics, no measurement and no claim that the tensor is realized by matter.

items.title: Acceleration, expansion and the along-congruence derivative of an observer congruence
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset carrying the restricted smooth
structure of
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]],
and let $n$ be a smooth observer congruence on $U$
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]), so that $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$
and $n_p$ is future-directed at every $p\in U$.

**(a) Acceleration.** The **acceleration field** of $n$ is the smooth vector
field

$$a:=\nabla_nn,$$

the covariant derivative of $n$ along itself; componentwise
$a^b=n^a\nabla_an^b$. The item defines the field; that it is spatial and that
it is the acceleration of the observer curves is proved in
[[lem-gr-congruence-acceleration-and-expansion-properties]].

**(b) Expansion.** The **expansion** of $n$ is the smooth function

$$\theta:=\nabla_an^a=g^{ab}\nabla_an_b .$$

Its chart formula and its identification with $h^{ab}\nabla_an_b$ are proved in
[[lem-gr-congruence-acceleration-and-expansion-properties]].

**(c) Along-congruence derivative.** For a smooth function
$f:U\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) define

$$Df:=n^a\nabla_af,$$

the derivative of $f$ along $n$; $Df$ is smooth and $D$ is a derivation of the
smooth functions on $U$
([[lem-gr-congruence-acceleration-and-expansion-properties]] clause (d)).

**(d) Scope.** The acceleration and the expansion are geometric data of the
congruence $n$ alone, computed with the connection $\nabla$. This item asserts
neither $a=0$ (a geodesic congruence) nor $\theta=0$, and it defines no shear,
vorticity, measurement, clock reading or physical interpretation; the reading
of observer curves as ideal-clock worldlines belongs to the framework's
postulates and is not asserted here.

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), sections 3.3.3-3.3.4: the Eulerian observer congruence, its 4-acceleration a = grad_n n and the identity a = D ln N, printed pp. 43-44 (PDF pp. 43-44), and sections 4.1.1 and 5.2: the divergence of the Eulerian normal and the conservation equation in which it appears, printed pp. 51 and 72-73 (PDF pp. 51 and 72-73)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3: covariant derivatives along a curve and the geodesic equation, printed pp. 67-69 and 100-101 (PDF pp. 74-76 and 107-108)

items.title: Spatiality and curve identity of the acceleration, the divergence form of the expansion, and the along-congruence derivative
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
subset and let $n$ be a smooth observer congruence on $U$, with acceleration
$a=\nabla_nn$, expansion $\theta=\nabla_an^a$ and along-congruence derivative
$D$ as in [[def-gr-congruence-acceleration-and-expansion]]. Then:

**(a) The acceleration is spatial.** $a$ is smooth and

$$g_p(a_p,n_p)=0\qquad\text{for every }p\in U,$$

that is, $a_p\in n_p^{\perp}$; equivalently $h(a)=a$ for the projection field
$h$ of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]].

**(b) Acceleration of the observer curves.** Let $\gamma:I\to U$ be an
observer curve of the congruence, that is, an integral curve of $n$
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]] clause (b)), and let
$D_s$ denote the covariant derivative along $\gamma$
([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]). Then

$$D_s\gamma'(s)=a_{\gamma(s)}\qquad\text{for every }s\in I .$$

Consequently every observer curve is a geodesic in its flow parameter if and
only if $a=0$ on $U$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(c) Divergence form of the expansion.** In every smooth chart of $U$, with
$g_{ab}$ the metric components and $w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}>0$,

$$\theta=w^{-1}\partial_a\bigl(w\,n^a\bigr),$$

and $\theta=g^{ab}\nabla_an_b=h^{ab}\nabla_an_b$ with
$h^{ab}=g^{ab}+n^an^b$. In particular $\theta$ is smooth.

**(d) Derivation property.** For smooth functions $f,h:U\to\mathbb R$,
$D(fh)=f\,Dh+h\,Df$, and $D$ annihilates constants.

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), sections 3.3.3-3.3.4: a = grad_n n and a = D ln N, and the relation grad n = -K - D ln N (x) n, printed pp. 43-44 (PDF pp. 43-44); sections 5.2.1-5.2.2: the expansion term in the energy conservation equation, printed pp. 72-73 (PDF pp. 72-73)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3: the covariant derivative along a curve, parallel transport and the geodesic equation, printed pp. 67-69 and 100-101 (PDF pp. 74-76 and 107-108)

items.title: Divergence of the measured energy-momentum current and the finite-chain balance identity
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
subset, let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$ with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $n$ be a smooth observer congruence on $U$.
Let $\mu$, $J$, $\Phi$, $S$ be the fields of
[[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]] and let $a$, $\theta$, $D$ be the
kinematic fields of [[def-gr-congruence-acceleration-and-expansion]].

**(a) Divergence identity.** On $U$,

$$\nabla_aJ^a=-T^{ab}\nabla_an_b .$$

**(b) Balance identity.** On $U$,

$$D\mu+\mu\theta+\nabla_a\Phi^a=-T^{ab}\nabla_an_b .$$

**(c) Finite-chain balance.** For this clause choose an orientation on $U$
and use its metric volume form $\mathrm{vol}_{g|_U}$, written $\mathrm{vol}_g$.
Let $C$ be a finite smooth singular $4$-chain of
$M$ contained in $U$ with induced boundary
$\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$, where $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$ are smooth
singular $3$-chains ([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause
(b)). Then

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(-T^{ab}\nabla_an_b\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if $T^{ab}\nabla_an_b=0$ on an open subset containing the image
of $C$, then $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$.

**(d) Killing contraction.** If $\xi$ is a smooth vector field on $U$ with
$\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0$ (a Killing field,
[[def-gr-killing-field]]), then $T^{ab}\nabla_a\xi_b=0$ on $U$.

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), sections 5.2.1-5.2.2: the 3+1 decomposition of the conservation equation and the energy conservation equation containing the expansion term, printed pp. 72-73 (PDF pp. 72-73)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.5: the failure of covariant conservation to produce a boundary term for the energy-momentum tensor, and the charge of the Killing current, printed pp. 187-189 (PDF pp. 194-196)
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 8.7: Stokes' theorem and the flux balance, printed pp. 109-110 (PDF pp. 110-111)

items.title: Kinematics of a timelike Killing congruence and conservation of the redshift-weighted energy current
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
subset, and let $\xi$ be a smooth Killing field on $U$
([[def-gr-killing-field]]) that is everywhere timelike and future-directed,

$$g_p(\xi_p,\xi_p)<0,\qquad g_p(\xi_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in U .$$

Put $X:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}:U\to(0,\infty)$ (the positive square root) and
$n:=\xi/X$, so that $n$ is a smooth observer congruence on $U$. Let $T$ be a
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$ with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, let $\mu$, $J$, $\Phi$, $S$ be the fields of
[[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]], and let $a$, $\theta$, $D$ be the
kinematic fields of [[def-gr-congruence-acceleration-and-expansion]]. Then:

**(a) Normalization is constant along the congruence, and the acceleration is
a spatial gradient.**

$$n^a\nabla_aX=0,\qquad a_a=\nabla_a\ln X=\frac{1}{X}\nabla_aX,$$

equivalently $\nabla_aX=Xa_a$ and $a=\nabla\ln X$ is the spatial gradient of
$\ln X$.

**(b) Vanishing expansion and symmetric part.** $\theta=0$ and

$$\nabla_an_b+\nabla_bn_a=-(n_aa_b+n_ba_a).$$

**(c) The divergence source is the acceleration term.**
$T^{ab}\nabla_an_b=J^aa_a=\Phi^aa_a$, and consequently

$$\nabla_aJ^a=-\Phi^aa_a .$$

**(d) Conservation of the redshift-weighted current.** On $U$,

$$\nabla_a(XJ^a)=0,\qquad \nabla_a\bigl(T^{ab}\xi_b\bigr)=0 .$$

For the following flux assertion choose an orientation on $U$ and the
volume form of the restricted metric. Then for every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$ of $M$ contained in
$U$ with induced boundary $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$,

$$\Phi_{XJ}(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_{XJ}(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_{XJ}(B),$$

where $\Phi_{XJ}$ is the flux of the smooth vector field $XJ$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b)).

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 5.3: Killing vectors, the equation nabla_a X_b + nabla_b X_a = 0 and conservation of X_a V^a along geodesics, printed pp. 53-56 (PDF pp. 54-57)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 5 (5.39)-(5.42): Killing vectors and the conserved quantity along geodesics, printed pp. 140-142 (PDF pp. 147-149)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), sections 4.3.3 and 4.5.5: the Killing current -K^mu T_{mu nu}, its divergence and the energy interpretation of its charge, printed pp. 165-166 and 188-189 (PDF pp. 172-173 and 195-196)

items.title: The Killing energy current and the Killing energy of a three-chain
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
subset carrying the restricted smooth structure of
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]],
choose an orientation on $U$ and its metric volume form (independent of the
time orientation), let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) — in an application this is the
stress-energy tensor field of the model's matter sector
([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]) — and let $\xi$ be a Killing field of
$(M,g)$ on $U$ ([[def-gr-killing-field]],
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a)) that is
everywhere timelike and future-directed,

$$g_p(\xi_p,\xi_p)<0,\qquad g_p(\xi_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in U .$$

Put $X:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ on $U$ and $n:=\xi/X$, an observer congruence on
$U$: $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,N)=g(\xi,N)/X<0$
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).

**(a) Killing current.** The **Killing current** of the pair $(T,\xi)$ is the
smooth vector field on $U$

$$J_\xi{}^a:=T^{ab}\xi_b .$$

Since $\xi=Xn$ and $J^a=-T^{ab}n_b$, one has
$T^{ab}\xi_b=-XJ^a$, where $J=-T(\cdot,n)$ is the measured
energy-momentum current of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]]; no
conservation of $J_\xi$ is asserted by this definition.

**(b) Killing energy of a three-chain.** For every finite smooth singular
$3$-chain $\Sigma$ of $M$ contained in $U$, the **Killing energy** of $\Sigma$
with respect to $\xi$ is the real number

$$Q_\xi(\Sigma):=-\Phi_{J_\xi}(\Sigma),$$

where $\Phi_{J_\xi}$ is the flux of the current $J_\xi$ through
$3$-chains on the oriented open submanifold $U$ in the sense of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]
clause (b).

**(c) Relation to the measured energy current.** Since $J_\xi=-XJ$,

$$Q_\xi(\Sigma)=\Phi_{XJ}(\Sigma),$$

the flux of the redshift-weighted measured energy current $XJ$. For a
$3$-simplex $\sigma$ that is non-null with velocity basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ and
adapted unit normal $\nu^{*}$ (so that $(\nu^{*},v_1,v_2,v_3)$ is positively
oriented and $\varepsilon:=g(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$), the pullback of
$\iota_{XJ}\mathrm{vol}_g$ is
$\varepsilon\,g(XJ,\nu^{*})\sqrt{|\det(g(v_i,v_j))|}\,dt^1\wedge dt^2\wedge dt^3$
([[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (c)); when
$\nu^{*}=-n$ and the $v_i$ span $n^{\perp}$ this coefficient equals
$-X\mu\sqrt{|\det(g(v_i,v_j))|}$, so up to the orientation sign carried by the
adapted normal, $Q_\xi(\Sigma)$ is the integral of the redshift-weighted
measured energy density $X\mu$ over $\Sigma$.

**(d) Reading and scope.** $Q_\xi(\Sigma)$ is read as the energy that the
model assigns to the chain $\Sigma$ under the symmetry $\xi$, in the framework
of the postulates [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]],
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] with the assigned tensor and symmetry; it does not require the field law
for its definition. Its numerical value is read in
$\mathrm J$ under the unit conventions of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]] when $T$ is read in
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. The value depends on the model, on $\xi$
(replacing $\xi$ by $\lambda\xi$ with constant $\lambda>0$ multiplies $X$,
$J_\xi$ and $Q_\xi$ by $\lambda$), and on the chain $\Sigma$. The definition
asserts no conservation, no positivity, no finiteness for unbounded chains and
no measured value. If additionally $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, the Killing
current lemma gives conservation up to the side flux. The field law
([[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] or [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]])
is one way to supply this divergence condition; it is not necessary for
the mathematical conservation implication. If no
timelike Killing field exists on $U$, $Q_\xi$ is not defined by this item.

references.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.5 'Conserved Energy from a Killing Vector': the current J_T = -K^mu T_{mu nu}, its vanishing divergence for Killing K, and the charge Q_T(Sigma) identified with the energy of the matter when K is everywhere timelike, printed pp. 188-189 (PDF pp. 195-196)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 5.3: Killing vectors and conserved quantities, printed pp. 53-56 (PDF pp. 54-57); section 9.3: conservation of T^{ab} on shell, printed pp. 116-118 (PDF pp. 117-119)
E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), section 4.1.2: energy density and momentum density measured by an observer, printed p. 52 (PDF p. 52)

items.physical_scope: The energy quantity associated with a timelike Killing symmetry of the smooth classical branch of the gravitational framework: the Killing current built from a smooth stress-energy tensor and its flux through finite smooth singular three-chains on a chosen oriented domain. The item fixes the object, its normalization and its model energy reading; it asserts no conservation, no finiteness for unbounded chains, no positivity and no measurement. With divergence-free T and Killing symmetry, the current lemma supplies conservation up to side flux; the field law is one possible source of that divergence condition. The definition applies only where the stated timelike Killing field exists.

items.title: Local energy balance of the measured current and conservation of the Killing energy in stationary models
items.statement:
Adopt one of the two presentations of the framework's field law,
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] or
[[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]], for a model with geometric data
and matter sector satisfying [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]; the two presentations define one
field law by [[pthm-gr-adopted-action-and-einstein-equations]]. Let $(M,g,N)$
be the model's smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, let $U\subseteq M$ be the matter domain with the induced orientation, let $T$ be the model's
smooth symmetric stress-energy tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]), and let $n$ be a smooth observer
congruence on $U$, read as the field of directions of ideal-clock observers of
the model ([[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]). Let $\mu$, $J$, $\Phi$, $S$
be the measured fields of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]], with the
physical reading and units of [[def-gr-measured-energy-density-flux-and-stress]]: $\Phi$ is the normalized spatial tensor current and its SI measured
energy-flux vector is $q=c\Phi$,
and let $a$, $\theta$, $D$ be the kinematic fields of
[[def-gr-congruence-acceleration-and-expansion]].

**(a) On-shell conservation.** The adopted field law implies

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\qquad\text{on }U .$$

**(b) Local energy balance.** On $U$,

$$D\mu+\mu\theta+\nabla_a\Phi^a=\nabla_aJ^a=-T^{ab}\nabla_an_b .$$

Thus the energy density measured by the congruence, its normalized spatial
current $\Phi$ (SI energy flux $q=c\Phi$) and its expansion obey a local balance whose source is the congruence term
$-T^{ab}\nabla_an_b$; the measured energy current is conserved on an open set
exactly where that source vanishes there.

**(c) Finite-chain bookkeeping.** For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain
$C$ of $M$ contained in $U$ with induced boundary
$\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$,

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(-T^{ab}\nabla_an_b\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if the source term vanishes on an open set containing the image
of $C$ and the side flux $\Phi_J(B)$ vanishes, then
$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)$: equal measured energy needs a vanishing
side flux, not merely on-shell conservation.

**(d) Stationary models and the Killing energy.** Suppose in addition that
$U$ carries a Killing field $\xi$ of $(M,g)$ that is everywhere timelike and
future-directed, with $X:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and $n=\xi/X$, and let
$Q_\xi$ be the Killing energy of
[[def-gr-killing-energy-charge]]. Then:

1. $\nabla_a(XJ^a)=0$ and $\nabla_a(T^{ab}\xi_b)=0$ on $U$.
2. For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C\subseteq U$ with
   $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$,

$$Q_\xi(\Sigma_2)-Q_\xi(\Sigma_1)=-Q_\xi(B);$$

   in particular, if $Q_\xi(B)=0$ then $Q_\xi(\Sigma_2)=Q_\xi(\Sigma_1)$: the
   model's energy assigned to homologous slices is conserved up to the side
   flux, and is conserved when that flux vanishes.
3. In this stationary case the measured energy current itself satisfies
   $\nabla_aJ^a=-\Phi^aa_a$ with $a=\nabla\ln X$, so
   $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $U$ if and only if $\Phi^aa_a=0$ there.

**(e) Qualification.** The theorem asserts no existence of a timelike Killing
field, no finiteness or convergence for chains outside the finite smooth
singular class, no asymptotic or quasilocal mass, no positivity of $\mu$, and
no measured value. Its conclusions are conditional on the adopted field law,
the stated smoothness and the stated chains; the theorem uses no empirical
premise, and any later use of a numerical energy must carry its own
measurement, calibration and uncertainty qualifications.

references.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.5 'The Slippery Business of Energy Conservation': covariant conservation of a current gives conserved charges only up to the boundary flux; covariant conservation of T is not actual conservation; the Killing current -K^mu T_{mu nu} has conserved charges interpreted as the energy of the matter for timelike K, printed pp. 187-189 (PDF pp. 194-196)

E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), section 5.2: the 3+1 energy conservation equation with the expansion term and the gravitational power source in the Newtonian limit, printed pp. 72-74 (PDF pp. 72-74); section 4.1.2: the measured energy density, momentum density and stress, printed p. 52 (PDF p. 52)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 9.3: on-shell conservation nabla_a T^{ab} = 0 as a consequence of the matter equations and diffeomorphism invariance, printed pp. 116-118 (PDF pp. 117-119)

items.physical_scope: The smooth classical branch of the adopted gravitational framework with the field law in one of its two presentations and a smooth matter stress-energy tensor on the model's matter domain: the local balance identity for the energy density, energy flux and energy-momentum current measured by a prescribed ideal-clock observer congruence, the finite-chain bookkeeping of that current, and, when the model admits an everywhere timelike future-directed Killing field, the conservation of the associated Killing energy up to the side flux. The theorem is a conditional consequence of the adopted field law and the stated smooth hypotheses; it asserts no existence of Killing fields, no convergence or finiteness for unbounded chains, no asymptotic or quasilocal mass, no positivity and no measured value, and it carries no empirical premise.

items.title: Absence of a universal global energy: observer dependence, no local gravitational energy, and deferred asymptotic masses
items.statement:
## Scope and status

This note fixes what the framework does and does not provide under the name
"energy". It proves nothing by itself and asserts no fact about nature.

- **Observer dependence of measured energy.** The measured energy density
  $\mu=T_{ab}n^an^b$ and the SI measured energy flux $q=c\Phi$ of
  [[def-gr-measured-energy-density-flux-and-stress]] depend on the observer
  congruence $n$; only the tensor $T$ itself is observer independent. For a
  prescribed model different congruences generally assign different energies
  to the same region, and the framework contains no congruence-independent
  local energy density of matter.

- **No local gravitational energy in the framework as built.** The framework
  defines a stress-energy tensor only for the matter sector
  ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]],
  [[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]): $T$ is the matter content of the
  field law, and the geometric side $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}$ has identically
  vanishing divergence ([[thm-gr-second-bianchi-and-divergence-free-einstein]]).
  The local balance of [[pthm-gr-local-energy-balance]] is a balance of the
  *matter* current; no item of the framework defines a local gravitational
  energy density or flux that would complete it into a conservation law for a
  total energy. The framework's normal-coordinate material
  ([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]],
  [[rem-gr-normal-coordinates-and-local-inertial-frames-scope]]) records that
  the connection can be made to vanish at a point by an adapted chart while
  the curvature data cannot be removed by that choice; this is recorded here
  only as the scope statement that no construction of a local gravitational
  energy density is available from the connection alone. It is not a no-go
  theorem, and no no-go theorem is claimed. The cited treatments record the
  corresponding physical point: a gauge-invariant local energy density of the
  linearized gravitational field is unavailable, and gravitational energy
  cannot be localized.

- **A global energy needs a symmetry and control of the flux.** The Killing
  energy $Q_\xi$ of [[def-gr-killing-energy-charge]] exists only for a model
  that admits an everywhere timelike future-directed Killing field $\xi$;
  a general metric has no nonzero Killing field beyond $\xi=0$
  ([[def-gr-killing-field]]). Even with such a $\xi$, the finite-chain
  statement of [[pthm-gr-local-energy-balance]] gives
  $Q_\xi(\Sigma_2)-Q_\xi(\Sigma_1)=-Q_\xi(B)$: conservation requires the side
  flux to vanish. For a slice of unbounded spatial extent one further needs
  the limiting flux and the integrals to converge; the flux theorem
  [[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] is stated for finite
  smooth singular chains and supplies no such limit, and the framework's scope
  note [[rem-gr-einstein-matter-scope-and-conventions]] already excludes
  arbitrary rough or noncompact domains from its smooth branch.

- **A Killing field need not be timelike everywhere.** A Killing field that is
  timelike on one region may be spacelike or past-directed elsewhere, in which
  case the charge is not an energy there; the de Sitter example recorded in the
  cited Tong reference has no globally defined positive conserved energy of
  this kind. Nothing in the framework selects a preferred Killing field or
  normalization: the normalization is part of the model data, and changing
  $\xi$ changes $Q_\xi$ as recorded in
  [[def-gr-killing-energy-charge]] clause (d).

- **Asymptotic and quasilocal masses are deferred.** The ADM energy and
  related Bondi-type quantities are defined by surface integrals at infinity
  for asymptotically flat spacetimes, and Komar-type integrals by fluxes at a
  chosen boundary; both require an asymptotic or boundary structure
  (fall-off conditions, a sphere at infinity, limit arguments) or a chosen
  quasilocal surface. None of this structure is defined on this page or on
  the pages it depends on. Such masses are deferred to a future
  boundary-asymptotic module; no asymptotic mass, quasilocal mass or
  radiative energy loss is defined, computed or used in this framework here.

- **Empirical status.** The note contains no experiment, no measured input and
  no empirical premise. It records the scope of the framework's energy
  statements and the obligations deferred to other pages; it does not assert
  that the framework's energy notions are the only possible ones, nor that
  the model describes nature.

Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.3.2 and section 4.5.5: the energy associated with a Killing vector, the de Sitter example in which the Killing field is timelike only in the static patch and there is no global positive conserved energy, and the failure of covariant conservation of T to give actual conservation, printed pp. 163 and 187-189 (PDF pp. 170 and 194-196); section 4.3.3: Komar integrals and their interpretation as the mass of the spacetime, printed pp. 165-167 (PDF pp. 172-174)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 7.5 'The energy in gravitational waves': the candidate quadratic tensor t_{mu nu} is not gauge invariant, 'the impossibility of localizing gravitational energy', and the ADM energy defined by a surface integral at infinity for asymptotically flat spacetimes, printed pp. 88-89 (PDF pp. 89-90)
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 4: the field equations and the energy-momentum tensor as matter content, printed pp. 116-118 (PDF pp. 123-125)

items.physical_scope: Scope and status note for energy questions of the classical gravitational framework: the observer dependence of measured energy density, the absence of any local gravitational energy density in the framework as built, the additional hypotheses a global energy requires, and the deferral of asymptotic masses. The note asserts no theorem about nature, no no-go theorem and no measured value.

items.title: Scope and status of the local-and-global-energy page: what is defined, what is conditional, and what is deferred
items.statement:
This note fixes the scope of the page's energy content and the status of its
claims; it proves nothing by itself.

- **What is defined.** For a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $T$
  and a smooth observer congruence $n$, the page defines the measured energy
  density, energy-momentum current, energy flux and spatial stress
  ([[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]]), their physical reading and
  units ([[def-gr-measured-energy-density-flux-and-stress]]), the acceleration
  and expansion of the congruence
  ([[def-gr-congruence-acceleration-and-expansion]]), and, for a model with an
  everywhere timelike future-directed Killing field, the Killing energy current
  and the Killing energy of a finite three-chain
  ([[def-gr-killing-energy-charge]]). The algebraic decomposition behind the
  measured fields is proved in
  [[lem-gr-observer-energy-momentum-decomposition]], and the divergence and
  finite-chain identities in
  [[lem-gr-energy-momentum-current-divergence]] and
  [[lem-gr-killing-congruence-kinematics-and-energy-current]].

- **What is conditional.** The local energy balance and the conservation of
  the Killing energy are theorem
  [[pthm-gr-local-energy-balance]]: they are conditional on the adopted field
  law, on the smooth hypotheses of
  [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
  [[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], and, for the conservation
  statement, on the existence of the timelike Killing field and on the
  vanishing of the side flux. Nothing on the page establishes that a Killing
  field exists for a given metric
  ([[def-gr-killing-field]],
  [[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]), and the finite-chain
  flux statements are those of
  [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and
  [[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]].

- **Smooth and finite branch.** All items assume smooth fields on an open
  domain and finite smooth singular chains; distributional sources,
  interfaces, noncompact or rough regions and asymptotic limits are outside
  the branch, in the sense of
  [[rem-gr-einstein-matter-scope-and-conventions]]. The observer congruence is
  an idealization of a family of ideal-clock worldlines; the physical reading
  of measured quantities is the framework's reading of
  [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]], and no numerical value is
  asserted by any item of the page.

- **Deferred obligations.** The absence of a universal global energy, the
  observer dependence of measured energy and the deferral of ADM-, Bondi- and
  Komar-type masses to a future boundary-asymptotic module are recorded in
  [[rem-gr-no-universal-global-energy]]. In particular, no asymptotic energy,
  quasilocal mass, radiative loss or initial-data energy is defined or used
  here. Later pages of this framework may consume the redshift-weighted
  Killing current and the measured-energy identities for stationary and
  spherical models and for linearized waves; each such use must verify the
  hypotheses of the items it consumes and carry the item's scope
  qualifications with it.

- **Choice convention.** The smooth-bundle structure used throughout the page
  assumes the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] through
  [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]] (and
  [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]]); no other choice principle is
  used, and no foundational item of this page introduces a choice principle of
  its own.

- **Empirical status.** The page contains no experiment, no measured input and
  no empirical premise. Its physics claims are conditional deductions from the
  adopted postulates and stated hypotheses; any later comparison with reported
  observations tests the combined model and apparatus assumptions and is
  evidence rather than proof.

references.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.5: covariant conservation of T is not actual conservation, and the Killing current yields conserved charges with an energy interpretation, printed pp. 187-189 (PDF pp. 194-196)
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 9.3: conservation of the energy-momentum tensor and its matter origin, printed pp. 116-118 (PDF pp. 117-119)

items.physical_scope: Scope, convention and status note for the energy material of the classical gravitational framework: the objects defined on this page, the status of the balance and conservation claims, the smooth and finite-chain restrictions, the choice assumptions, and the obligations deferred to other pages. The note asserts no theorem, no measured value and no claim about nature.

items.title: A translating dust in flat space: measured energy density, flux and the local balance
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart, the flat metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the time orientation $N=\partial_0$, with the standard coordinate
orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and
the metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let
$\beta\in(-1,1)$, put $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, let
$\varphi:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth, and define

$$\rho(x):=\varphi\bigl(x^1-\beta x^0\bigr),\qquad u:=\gamma\bigl(\partial_0+\beta\partial_1\bigr).$$

Further let $n:=\partial_0$, and let $T^{ab}:=\rho\,u^au^b$ (the tensor of the
dust model $(\rho,u)$, [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]). Then:

1. $u$ is a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field and $(\rho,u)$
   is a dust model on $M$; the dust system holds, so $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on
   $M$.
2. $n$ is a smooth observer congruence with $a=\nabla_nn=0$ and
   $\theta=\nabla_an^a=0$.
3. The measured fields of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]] for the
   congruence $n$ are

$$\mu=\rho\gamma^2,\qquad J=\rho\gamma^2\bigl(\partial_0+\beta\partial_1\bigr),\qquad \Phi=\rho\gamma^2\beta\,\partial_1,\qquad S=\rho\gamma^2\beta^2\,\partial_1\otimes\partial_1,$$

   and they satisfy the decomposition
   $T^{ab}=\mu\,n^an^b+n^a\Phi^b+n^b\Phi^a+S^{ab}$ of
   [[lem-gr-observer-energy-momentum-decomposition]] clause (b).
4. $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $M$, and the local balance of
   [[lem-gr-energy-momentum-current-divergence]] clause (b) holds:

$$D\mu+\mu\theta+\nabla_a\Phi^a=0=-T^{ab}\nabla_an_b .$$

   In this example the balance is the continuity equation for the translating
   density current $\rho\gamma(\partial_0+\beta\partial_1)$.

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), section 5.2: the 3+1 energy conservation equation with the expansion term, and the Newtonian limit linearised check, printed pp. 72-74 (PDF pp. 72-74)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), sections 4.5.3-4.5.4: the dust and perfect fluid energy-momentum tensors and the equations equivalent to their conservation, printed pp. 183-187 (PDF pp. 190-194)
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 (1.104)-(1.106): the energy-momentum tensor of dust and its conservation, printed pp. 28-30 (PDF pp. 35-37)

items.title: A boost-Killing congruence in flat space: acceleration source and conservation of the redshift-weighted energy current
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart, the flat metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the time orientation $N=\partial_0$, with the standard coordinate
orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let

$$U:=\bigl\{p\in M:\ x^1(p)>|x^0(p)|\bigr\},\qquad \xi:=x^1\partial_0+x^0\partial_1,$$

let $X:=\sqrt{(x^1)^2-(x^0)^2}>0$ on $U$, let $n:=\xi/X$, and let
$T^{ab}:=\rho\,\partial_0^a\partial_0^b$ with $\rho>0$ constant (the tensor of
the dust model $(\rho,\partial_0)$, [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]). Then:

1. $U$ is open, $\xi$ is a Killing field on $U$, and $n$ is a smooth
   future-directed observer congruence on $U$ with
   $n^a\nabla_aX=0$ and acceleration and expansion

$$a=\nabla\ln X=\frac{x^0}{X^2}\,\partial_0+\frac{x^1}{X^2}\,\partial_1,\qquad \theta=0 .$$

2. $(\rho,\partial_0)$ satisfies the dust system and
   $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $M$.
3. The measured fields of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]] for the
   congruence $n$ are

$$\mu=\rho\frac{(x^1)^2}{X^2},\qquad J=\rho\frac{x^1}{X}\,\partial_0,\qquad \Phi=-\rho\frac{x^1(x^0)^2}{X^3}\,\partial_0-\rho\frac{(x^1)^2x^0}{X^3}\,\partial_1 .$$

4. $\nabla_aJ^a=-\Phi^aa_a=\rho x^0x^1/X^3$ and
   $D\mu+\mu\theta+\nabla_a\Phi^a=\rho x^0x^1/X^3$: the balance of
   [[lem-gr-energy-momentum-current-divergence]] clause (b) holds with a
   nonvanishing acceleration source, so the measured energy current is *not*
   conserved.
5. $XJ=\rho x^1\partial_0$ satisfies $\nabla_a(XJ^a)=0$ and
   $T^{ab}\xi_b=-XJ^a$: the redshift-weighted current is conserved, in
   accordance with [[lem-gr-killing-congruence-kinematics-and-energy-current]]
   clause (d). Consequently, for every finite smooth singular $4$-chain
   $C\subseteq U$ with $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$, the flux
   $\Phi_{XJ}$ satisfies $\Phi_{XJ}(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_{XJ}(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_{XJ}(B)$;
   in particular $\Phi_{XJ}(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_{XJ}(\Sigma_1)$ whenever the
   velocity vectors of every simplex of $B$ span a hyperplane containing
   $\partial_0$.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 5.3: Killing vectors, the Killing equation and conserved quantities along geodesics, printed pp. 53-56 (PDF pp. 54-57)
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 5: Killing vectors and the boost symmetry of Minkowski space, printed pp. 140-142 (PDF pp. 147-149)

E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), sections 3.3.3-3.3.4: the acceleration of an Eulerian congruence as the gradient of the logarithm of the lapse, printed pp. 43-44 (PDF pp. 43-44)

items.title: The perfect-fluid energy equation recovered from the local energy balance
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
subset and let $(\varepsilon,p,n)$ be a perfect-fluid model on $U$ with
stress-energy tensor $T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+p)n^an^b+pg^{ab}$
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]); suppose
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Take the observer congruence of
[[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]] to be the fluid field $n$ itself,
and write $D=n^a\nabla_a$ and $\theta=\nabla_an^a$. Then:

1. For this congruence $\mu=\varepsilon$, $J=\varepsilon n$, $\Phi=0$ and
   $S^{ab}=p\,h^{ab}$ with $h^{ab}=g^{ab}+n^an^b$.
2. $T^{ab}\nabla_an_b=p\theta$, so the local balance of
   [[lem-gr-energy-momentum-current-divergence]] clause (b) reads

$$\nabla_a(\varepsilon n^a)=-p\theta,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\theta=0 .$$

3. This is exactly the energy equation of
   [[prop-gr-dust-and-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]] clause (b) under
   the hypothesis $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$; the momentum (Euler) equation is the
   complementary projection of $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ and is not implied by the
   energy balance alone.

references.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.4: the perfect fluid tensor (4.53) and the conservation equations (4.54)-(4.55) as energy conservation and the Euler equation, printed pp. 185-187 (PDF pp. 192-194)

E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), section 5.2.2: the energy conservation equation containing the expansion term, printed p. 73 (PDF p. 73), and section 5.3: the perfect-fluid 3+1 equations, printed pp. 75-76 (PDF pp. 75-76)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 6.2: the perfect fluid energy-momentum tensor (6.30) and conservation equations (6.31), printed pp. 65-66 (PDF pp. 66-67)

items.title: The Killing energy of a static dust in flat space and its conservation across slices
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart, the flat metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the time orientation $N=\partial_0$ and the
chart orientation, with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Let $\xi:=\partial_0$, let $\rho>0$ be
constant with the framework reading $\rho=\varepsilon$ in
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ (rest-mass density $\rho_m=\rho/c^2$),
let $u:=\partial_0$ and let $T^{ab}:=\rho\,u^au^b$, the tensor of the
dust model $(\rho,u)$ ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]). Then:

1. $\xi$ is a Killing field on $M$ that is everywhere timelike and
   future-directed, with $X=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}=1$ and congruence
   $n=\xi$; and the dust system holds, so $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $M$.
2. The Killing current of [[def-gr-killing-energy-charge]] is
   $J_\xi{}^a=T^{ab}\xi_b=-\rho\,\partial_0^a$, and its current $3$-form is
   $\iota_{J_\xi}\mathrm{vol}_g=-\rho\,dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.
3. For every finite smooth singular $3$-chain $\Sigma$ of $M$ whose simplices
   have chart velocity vectors $(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)$ at every
   parameter point — in particular for simplices parametrized by the spatial chart
   coordinates on a constant-$x^0$ slice — the Killing energy of
   $\Sigma$ is

$$Q_\xi(\Sigma)=\rho\int_\Sigma dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3,$$

   the integral of the model's rest-energy-density form over the chain in the
   framework's unit reading.
4. For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$ of $M$ with
   $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$,

$$Q_\xi(\Sigma_2)-Q_\xi(\Sigma_1)=-Q_\xi(B);$$

   in particular $Q_\xi(\Sigma_2)=Q_\xi(\Sigma_1)$ whenever the velocity
   vectors of every simplex of $B$ span a hyperplane containing $\partial_0$,
   since then the side flux vanishes.
5. Consequently this prescribed flat-source calculation realizes a
   conserved Killing charge: it is $\rho$ times the
   coordinate-volume reading of the slice region, read as the model's rest
   energy. The prescribed nonzero dust source is not asserted to solve the
   gravitational field law on this flat metric. No measured value is asserted.

references.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.5: the current -K^mu T_{mu nu} of a timelike Killing vector and its charge identified with the energy of the matter, printed pp. 188-189 (PDF pp. 195-196)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 (1.104)-(1.106): the energy-momentum tensor of dust, printed pp. 28-30 (PDF pp. 35-37); Ch. 5 (5.39)-(5.42): Killing vectors and conserved quantities, printed pp. 140-142 (PDF pp. 147-149)

items.physical_scope: An exact flat-space instance of the framework's Killing energy: a constant static dust with the translation Killing field of the identity chart, the current three-form of its Killing current, the value of the Killing energy on three-chains carried by constant-time slices, and its conservation up to the side flux. The example is an exact model calculation under the framework's unit reading; it asserts no measured value and no empirical mass, and the identification of its numbers with any physical energy requires separate empirical premises.

items.title: The measured energy density of a fixed tensor depends on the observer congruence
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "Let $U$ be a nonempty open subset of a time-oriented smooth
Lorentzian four-manifold and let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $U$. If $n$ and $n'$ are smooth observer congruences on
$U$, then the measured energy densities of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]]
agree, $T_{ab}n^an^b=T_{ab}n'^an'^b$ on $U$."

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), section 4.1.2: the energy density E = T(n,n) is the density measured by the Eulerian observer, so it is tied to the chosen normal n, printed p. 52 (PDF p. 52)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.3: T_{mu nu}u^mu u^nu = rho is the energy density measured by an observer comoving with the fluid, printed p. 186 (PDF p. 193)

items.physical_scope: A flat-space kinematic counterexample in the framework's reading: the energy density assigned by the observer split of a fixed smooth symmetric tensor depends on the chosen observer congruence, shown for a static dust tensor measured by a static and by a boosted congruence. The statement refuted is the observer independence of the measured energy density in the smooth branch; no dynamics, no conservation, no measurement and no empirical claim is involved.

items.title: A divergence-free symmetric tensor with negative measured energy density
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the flat metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the identity chart, with metric-selected
connection $\nabla$, and let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
field on an open subset $U\subseteq M$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Then
the measured energy density of [[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]] is
nonnegative, $T_{ab}n^an^b\ge0$ on $U$ for every smooth observer congruence
$n$ on $U$."

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 4: the Weak Energy Condition (4.72) as an additional assumption on T, printed p. 118 (PDF p. 125)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.7: the energy conditions are additional assumptions on the stress-energy tensor, printed pp. 194-198 (PDF pp. 201-205)

items.physical_scope: A flat-space pointwise counterexample in the framework's reading: a smooth symmetric tensor with vanishing divergence whose measured energy density is negative for a static observer congruence. It refutes the claim that on-shell conservation alone forces nonnegative measured energy density; no dynamics, no solution of any field equation, no measurement and no empirical claim is involved.
